nearbyCountiesFullText.nwsHeadline: AIR QUALITY ALERT IN EFFECT FROM 6 PM THIS EVENING TO 10 AM EST WEDNESDAY
nearbyCountiesFullText.description:
The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management
have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory for Elkhart County, in
effect from 6 PM this evening to 10 AM EST Wednesday.

A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM 2.5 has been issued due to
stagnant conditions and calm winds. Fine particulate levels are
expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups range. Active
children and adults, and people with respiratory disease, such as
asthma should limit prolonged outdoor exposure.

Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings
in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid
exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors closed as
much as possible.

For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at:

http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/

FXUS63 KIWX 171807
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
107 PM EST Tue Nov 17 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Tranquil fall weather continues with mild temperatures, light 
  winds, and sunshine this week!

- Rain chances hold off until Saturday night into Sunday (20-50% 
  chances).

- Mild weather pattern persists at least through the end of
  November.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 106 PM EST Tue Nov 17 2026

A large upper level ridge will amplify into the Midwest and Great 
Lakes regions throughout the coming week with temperatures remaining 
very mild by mid to late November standards. Surface high pressure 
will prevail with little movement from where it is currently 
centered over the Appalachian mountains. One more night with 
lows around freezing is expected tonight, with clear skies and 
light southerly winds promoting at least some localized patchy 
fog for Wednesday morning. Otherwise, temperatures will continue
to climb each day this week. Southerly flow and increased WAA 
will funnel in much warmer air from the Gulf and southern US. 
High temperatures will soar into the mid to upper 60s by late in
the week, which is 15 to 20 degrees above normal for this time 
of the year!

As the ridge breaks down by late in the week, rain chances return by 
Saturday night into Sunday with the passage of a cold front. Given 
that this is several days away, the overall pattern evolution may 
change. There are still uncertainties as to how much moisture this 
front will have to work with so low to medium PoPs persist with 20-
40% chances. Following the frontal passage, temperatures will 
moderate back towards seasonable levels with highs in the 40s. There 
are no real signs of winter yet as the mild weather pattern looks to 
hold at least through the end of meteorological fall. 


&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS THROUGH 18Z WEDNESDAY/...
Issued at 1106 AM EST Tue Nov 17 2026

High pressure will continue to support VFR conditions and light
winds through the TAF cycle. Could once again see patchy ground
fog toward daybreak tomorrow, though point probabilities remain
too low for a mention at this time.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...Air Quality Alert from 6 PM this evening to 10 AM EST 
     Wednesday for INZ005.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Johnson
AVIATION...Steinwedel

spc.summary: Organized severe thunderstorms are not forecast across the contiguous U.S. through tonight, although occasional strong/gusty winds may occur with convection across parts of coastal northern California, the Great Basin/Intermountain West, and south Florida.
spc.text:
SPC AC 171625

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1025 AM CST Tue Nov 17 2026

   Valid 171630Z - 181200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Organized severe thunderstorms are not forecast across the
   contiguous U.S. through tonight, although occasional strong/gusty
   winds may occur with convection across parts of coastal northern
   California, the Great Basin/Intermountain West, and south Florida.

   ...Coastal Northern California...
   A low-topped convective line will approach and move onshore along
   the northern CA Coast late tonight into early Wednesday morning
   (18/06-12Z). Low/mid-level flow will markedly increase in this time
   frame, as a mid/upper-level low moves across the eastern Pacific.
   There is some concern that strong/convectively augmented wind gusts
   could occur with this activity, primarily along the immediate coast
   of northern CA. But, MUCAPE will likely remain minimal/shallow (less
   than 200 J/kg), and perhaps even insufficient for lighting
   production due to the poor low-level moisture recovery forecast
   ahead of the convective band. Have not included low severe wind
   probabilities with this update due to the expected thermodynamic
   limitations, but strong/gusty winds locally exceeding the enhanced
   background gradient wind field may occur.

   ...Great Basin/Intermountain West...
   A highly amplified upper trough will continue to advance eastward
   across the Great Basin/Four Corners today. Cool surface temperatures
   and meager low-level moisture (surface dewpoints generally in the
   30s/40s) will hinder any more than weak instability from developing
   with filtered daytime heating. Still, with enhanced low/mid-level
   flow attendant to the ejecting upper trough overspreading these
   regions, some potential for gusty winds may exist with isolated to
   scattered convection that develops and spreads east-northeastward
   this afternoon/evening across northern AZ into eastern UT/western
   CO. Regardless, instability is expected to remain too meager to
   support organized severe thunderstorms.

   ...Florida...
   Recent water vapor satellite imagery shows a weak/positively tilted
   upper trough over the Southeast and eastern Gulf, with associated
   thunderstorms occurring well west of the Keys. Latest visible
   satellite imagery also suggests a remnant front/boundary extending
   eastward from this ongoing convection across the FL Straits.
   Isolated to scattered thunderstorms are anticipated through the
   period over the FL Atlantic Coast into south FL and the Keys in a
   weakly unstable but moderately sheared environment. However, poor
   lapse rates and multiple temperature inversions aloft noted on the
   12Z KEY/MFL observed soundings will likely hinder robust updrafts,
   and should limit overall severe potential.

   ..Gleason/Flournoy.. 11/17/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 2000Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 171704

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1104 AM CST Tue Nov 17 2026

   Valid 181200Z - 191200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are not expected Wednesday.

   ...Synopsis...
   Cool and stable conditions will preclude thunderstorm chances for
   much of the country on Wednesday. Isolated to scattered
   thunderstorms will mainly be confined to portions of the West Coast
   and along the FL peninsula. Across the West, an upper wave off the
   CA/OR coast is evident in late-morning water-vapor imagery. This
   feature will progress southward along the CA coast over the next 48
   hours. As this occurs, cold mid-level temperatures atop an
   adequately warm/moist marine layer will support sufficient buoyancy
   for shallow convection. Strong flow through much of the column may
   allow for a few stronger gusts with the deeper convective cores;
   however, such gusts will likely be comparable to ambient
   gradient-driven wind gusts. 

   Further east, a meandering upper low over the Gulf will continue to
   weaken through Thursday morning. South/southeasterly flow within the
   warm advection branch of the decaying cyclone will promote northward
   moisture flux and scattered to widespread showers and thunderstorms.
   Weakening flow through the CAPE-bearing layer should limit overall
   storm longevity and organization - especially inland where buoyancy
   profiles will be more modest.

   ..Moore.. 11/17/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0700Z

spc.summary: Thunderstorms are possible over portions of California, the Great Basin, and into the Southeast.
spc.text:
SPC AC 170828

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0228 AM CST Tue Nov 17 2026

   Valid 191200Z - 201200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorms are possible over portions of California, the Great
   Basin, and into the Southeast.

   ...Synopsis...
   A deep upper low will move inland across central CA Thursday as
   ridging persist over the eastern US. Onshore flow will favor
   thunderstorm potential across CA and parts of the Great Basin ahead
   of the upper low. Additionally, a weak vort max will linger across
   the Gulf producing unsettled weather. Elsewhere, high pressure will
   keep cool, dry and stable conditions in place over much of the
   country.

   ...CA Central Valley...
   Strong ascent beneath the upper-low and an associated 70+ kt jet
   will overspread central CA as a surface low moves onshore early
   Thursday. The low will aid inland transport of Pacific moisture
   which should allow for surface dewpoints to increase from the upper
   40s to low 50s F from the CA coast into the Central Valley. This,
   combined with steeping mid-level lapse rates and cold mid-level
   temperatures (500mb -25 to -30 C) should result in some
   destabilization and thunderstorm potential.

   Model soundings show shallow unstable thermodynamic profiles across
   the Central Valley with elongated hodographs from strong flow aloft.
   This may allow support a few stronger low-topped cells or clusters
   with non-zero severe potential. However, uncertainty on the degree
   of destabilization remains quite high as substantial cloud cover is
   likely. Given the uncertainty, severe probabilities will be withheld
   for this outlook.

   ...Southeast...
   A weak upper-level disturbance will continue to linger over the
   Southeast allowing for another day of scattered showers and
   thunderstorms. Buoyancy and lapse rates will remain modest, which
   should limit overall convective intensity. However, an isolated
   damaging gust cannot be completely ruled out over portions of
   southern GA into the FL Peninsula where scattered thunderstorm
   coverage is expected.

   ..Lyons.. 11/17/2026

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 3 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1930Z

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
